test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A bus travelling at 48 km/hr completes a journey in 9 hours. What should be its speed to cover the same distance in 12 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time ratio (T₁ : T₂) = 9 : 12 = 3 : 4

Speed ratio (S₁ : S₂) = 4 : 3

Given 4 units → 48 km/hr

New speed (3 units) → 12 × 3 = 36 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial speed (S₁) = 48 km/hr

Initial time (T₁) = 9 hours

New time (T₂) = 12 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

New Speed = Distance ÷ New Time

 
• 
 
 
 

 Case 1: S = 48 km/hr, T = 9 hours
 

 Case 2: S = ? , T = 12 hours
 Distance is Constant

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = S₁ × T₁

⇒ Total Distance = 48 × 9 = 432 km

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = Distance ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 432 ÷ 12

⇒ S₂ = 36 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, the average speed becomes 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |a − b|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = a + b.

Proportionality in Speed, Distance and Time

When Distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1 / T). When Time is constant, Distance is directly proportional to Speed (D ∝ S).
